text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bunds, futures off session lows but still down after U.S. Aug non-farm payrolls up 250,000, in line with expectations, jobless rate lowest since March 1989. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 97.28, up 0.06 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts crept back into positive territory to settle higher, buoyed by a small rally in U.S. Treasuries, trader said gilts were breathing a sigh of relief after nervousness surrounding U.S. payroll data, which came in slightly above market expectations at 250,000. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-04/32, up 03/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures survived their initial jitters after the U.S. non-farm payrolls release, taking their cue from the Treasury market, to settle at the day's high, a combination of short covering, relief that the jobs rise was not as bad as some had feared, a late franc rally and a positive response to French tax cut plans buoyed the market. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 123.64, up 0.16 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to firmer levels in late afternoon trade helped by the strength of the dollar and lira while support came from stronger T-bonds and German bunds. U.S. August jobs figures showed stronger jobs growth than expected but a temporary fall in T-bonds soon rebounded. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 115.92, up 0.50 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries continue to rise, trade at day's highs, dealer activity, strong foreign central bank buying and short-covering seen providing the market underpinning, short-covering sparked after street was seen mostly oversold ahead of August payrolls data, retailers mostly out. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-11/32, up 13/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.12 percent.

JAPAN - Large-lot speculative buying in the September Japanese government bond (JGB) futures drove them up to the day's high at their expiry on Friday, giving a boost to the key December contract as well. "It's a strange market. Everybody was watching the last several minutes of wild movements in the September before its expiry (at 0600 GMT)," said a senior bank trader. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 120.68, up 0.08 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - New issue activity was predictably slack with investors hugging the sidelines before the the U.S. jobs report, but while there was little issuance, next week's planned activity moved into slightly sharper focus. The Export-Import Bank of Korea will hold investor roadshows in London on Monday ahead of a planned $500 million five-year deal via Nomura International and SBC Warburg.
